import pandas as pd


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    postings = inputs["postings"].copy()

    # Preserve legacy cursor ordering: account_id, post_date, post_seq
    df = postings.sort_values(
        by=["account_id", "post_date", "post_seq"],
        kind="mergesort"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    # Determine validity per legacy TRY block logic
    valid = (
        df["qty"].notna()
        & (df["qty"] > 0)
        & df["unit_price"].notna()
        & (df["unit_price"] >= 0)
    )

    df["_valid"] = valid
    df["post_value"] = df["qty"] * df["unit_price"]

    # Only valid rows get posted; running_total is cumulative sum
    # of post_value within each account, computed only over valid rows,
    # in the sorted (account_id, post_date, post_seq) order.
    posted = df.loc[df["_valid"]].copy()
    posted["running_total"] = posted.groupby("account_id", sort=False)["post_value"].cumsum()

    posted_totals = posted[
        ["account_id", "post_seq", "post_date", "post_value", "running_total"]
    ].reset_index(drop=True)

    # Reject counts: one row per account seen in POSTINGS (including zero rejects),
    # preserving first-appearance order (mirrors flush-on-account-change + final flush).
    reject_series = df.groupby("account_id", sort=False)["_valid"].apply(
        lambda s: int((~s).sum())
    )
    reject_counts = reject_series.reset_index()
    reject_counts.columns = ["account_id", "reject_count"]
    reject_counts["reject_count"] = reject_counts["reject_count"].astype(int)

    return {
        "posted_totals": posted_totals,
        "reject_counts": reject_counts,
    }
